rv.q: The writing shows the dexterity of an escapologist in discovering new room within the cramped space of Holmes and Houdini apocrypha.
David Haig’s thoughtful, engaging drama has two 1920s pop-culture titans grapple with themes of faith, fraud and self-deception
The subject matter is intriguing, and performances are strong, particularly from Haig and Fraser, but its plodding pace and under-executed Vaudevillian concept leave you feeling short-changed.
With stellar acting, a superb script and thrilling design, you really won't want to miss this absolute treat of a production.
